transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um… mostly my eating, I guess. The last few weeks I just haven’t been eating much—skipping breakfast and lunch without really meaning to, then barely picking at dinner. My wife noticed too. My jeans are feeling kind of loose.
Are you avoiding food because you’re worried about gaining weight?

No, not really. It’s not about gaining weight. I just… haven’t been hungry, I guess. I’ll skip breakfast and lunch without meaning to, and then at dinner I kind of just pick at it. My jeans are getting looser, so I noticed.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
Yeah… I think so. Most days lately I wake up feeling kind of heavy and flat. Like the apartment’s just too quiet, and even playing guitar doesn’t really… do much.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
I don’t know… maybe a little. Stuff just doesn’t really grab me the same way lately. I haven’t felt like doing much.
Did something stressful happen in your life around the time this started?
I mean… nothing huge, I guess. It kind of started maybe three weeks ago, around when my wife got settled into her full-time work schedule. Since then it’s just been… like this.
Do you feel this started mainly as a reaction to your wife being away more because of her new full-time work schedule?
Maybe. I’m not sure it’s just that, but… yeah, it started around then. It’s been about three weeks, since she got into that full-time schedule.
Has this been making it hard for you to function day to day?
A little, yeah. I’m still doing the basic stuff around the house, but… my own projects have kind of stopped. And I’ve let a few chances slip with musicians I’d reached out to.
Have you been feeling unusually anxious or worried lately?
Not really… I mean, not unusually anxious. I worry some, but I haven’t noticed it being a big thing lately.
Have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?
No… not really. I mean, I’ve felt down, but I haven’t been thinking about hurting myself.
Have you been having trouble sleeping lately?
Yeah… a bit. I’m sleeping, but it’s not really solid. I’ll wake up around four or five, usually thinking about bills or tracks I haven’t finished, and then I’m already tired when the day starts.
Have you been having trouble concentrating lately?
Yeah… a little. I’ll try to work on some code or a track, and I just end up rereading the same line or replaying the same few bars over and over. Then I still can’t really figure out what to do next.
Have you been feeling worthless or guilty lately?
I don’t know… not really worthless. Maybe I get frustrated with myself, but I wouldn’t say guilty, exactly.
When your wife is home with you, do you feel noticeably less down?
Maybe a little, but… not really a lot. Most days I still wake up feeling kind of heavy and flat. Even if she’s there, it doesn’t fully shake that feeling.
Lately, have you been moving or talking noticeably slower than usual?
Yeah… I think so. Everything just feels kind of slowed down. I’ll sit there with my laptop open for a long time before I even start typing or plug anything in.
Do you feel down for most of the day, nearly every day?
Yeah… most days, I think. I usually wake up with this heavy, flat feeling, and the apartment feels really quiet. Even picking up my guitar doesn’t really do much.
Have you had any times lately when you felt unusually energetic or up, even for a short while?

Yeah… before this low stretch, there was a bit where I felt kind of fired up. Not exactly happy, but like I was on a roll, and any little interruption would really irritate me. I’d snap faster than usual.
During that fired-up period, did you need less sleep than usual?
Yeah. For a few nights I was only sleeping maybe three or four hours, but I’d wake up feeling… wired, I guess. Like sleeping was just kind of in the way.
During that wired period, were you more productive or starting a lot more projects than usual?

Yeah… I guess so. I started doing a lot at once—making lists of musicians to contact, sending messages, putting together pitch decks, trying to plan collaborations. It was all in the same week, which is… more than I’d normally take on.
During that wired period, did you feel unusually confident or like you had special abilities or ideas beyond your usual self?

Yeah… I guess I did. I felt like I’d kind of figured out the whole music-tech angle, like if I could just get people to hear the pitch, it could turn into a real career really fast. Looking back, that was probably more confidence than I usually have.
About how many days did that wired, fired-up period last?
I’m not totally sure… maybe several days? It kind of blurs together. I don’t remember the exact number.
